entries.title: Stuck at the Claude sign-in terminal window
entries.sub: The black window is the sign-in — here is exactly what to press
symptoms: what do I do with the terminal
steps: The black terminal window IS the sign-in — the Claude desktop app is a separate product and does not connect the Trade Companion.
If it asks "Do you trust this folder?" — press Enter on "Yes, I trust this folder". That's your own home folder; this is normal.
If you see a sign-in wizard: choose "Claude account with subscription" and finish in the browser.
If it opens to a normal prompt instead (you've used Claude Code before): type /login and press Enter, then choose "Claude account with subscription".
Make sure the browser that opens is signed into claude.ai with the same account as your subscription, then approve.
Close the terminal when it says you're logged in — the Claude light turns green by itself within a few seconds.

entries.title: "Connection port live" stays red
entries.sub: TradingView must be started by the app — not from its own shortcut
steps: This light is about TradingView, not Claude — TradingView must be STARTED BY THE APP so the two can talk.
Close TradingView completely (check the system tray — right-click the TradingView icon and quit).
Press the button below (or "Launch TradingView" in the sidebar).
The light goes green within seconds of TradingView finishing its load.
Every time you restart TradingView, launch it from the app again — a normally-started TradingView can never connect.

entries.title: "TradingView running" is red
entries.sub: TradingView Desktop is not open yet
steps: TradingView Desktop isn't open. The button below starts it the connected way.
No TradingView Desktop installed yet? Download it free from tradingview.com/desktop, install, then come back and use the button below (not the desktop shortcut).

entries.title: "Engine installed" is red
entries.sub: Usually an antivirus quarantine on a fresh install
steps: Part of the app's install is missing — this is usually an antivirus quarantine on a fresh install.
Open Windows Security → Protection history, and restore anything quarantined from the tv-command-hub folder.
If nothing shows there, reinstall the app from your original download link — the installer restores everything.
Still red after a reinstall? Use "Report to PDT" on any failed tool in chat so the details reach the developer.

entries.title: "Could not start TradingView: spawn EPERM"
entries.sub: Windows blocked the launch — fixed automatically in v0.2.98 and later
steps: TradingView now ships for Windows as a Microsoft Store style package, which installs into a protected folder. On most machines the app can start it normally, but on some accounts Windows refuses the launch and reports "spawn EPERM".

FIRST: make sure you are on v0.2.98 or later (the ? menu shows your version). From v0.2.98 the app detects the refusal and starts TradingView the way Windows wants instead — no action needed from you. Restart the app to pick up the update, then press the button below.
If you are on v0.2.98+ and it still fails, start TradingView yourself with the connection port open. Close TradingView completely, open PowerShell, and paste this one line:
Start-Process -FilePath "shell:AppsFolder\TradingView.Desktop_n534cwy3pjxzj!TradingView.Desktop" -ArgumentList "--remote-debugging-port=9222"
Wait for TradingView to finish loading, then open the Trade Companion — both "TradingView running" and "Connection port live" should be green, and you can skip the Launch button.

Starting TradingView from its normal shortcut or Start menu will NOT work — that opens it without the connection port, which is why the port light stays red even though TradingView is clearly running.

entries.title: Everything is green but chat replies with an error
entries.sub: Expired sign-ins and plan limits look like app problems — they aren't
symptoms: not logged in error in chat
steps: Click the Claude status light even if it looks connected — if it's yellow, your sign-in expired: run the sign-in again (terminal → /login → Claude account with subscription).
If chat mentions usage limits, your Claude plan hit its cap — it resets on Claude's schedule; the app itself is fine.
If a specific tool keeps failing, click "Report to PDT" on the failed tool — the report carries the technical details automatically.
